about: Grrr is a glossy, 3D-rendered red smiley from the early internet era, glaring sideways with heavy brows, bared clenched teeth and two white cartoon gloves balled into fists on either side of its face. It looks like an emoji that is one comment away from flipping a table. People use it to show petty, bottled-up anger: the irritation you feel over something small that you cannot really complain about out loud, like a slow walker or a vague reply.
origin: The image is a stock animated angry emoticon of the type common on forums and chat programs in the 2000s. It resurfaced as a blank template on imgflip under the title grrr.
usage:
Put the trigger in the top box, phrased as "when someone..." or a quote, and the bottom box finishes the trigger or adds a small, petty reaction. The emoji's balled fists do the rest, so the text can be very short.

The smaller the annoyance, the funnier the rage looks. Good targets: replies like "k", people saying "calm down", someone spoiling a show, a teammate stealing your kill, a meeting that could have been an email. Two or three words per line is plenty.
